transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-16
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Halo, Head of Platform), Liam O'Neill (Halo, ML Engineer), Carlos Mendes (Halo, CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): quickstart, credits, dedicated, private, vpc, pilot

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. I'm Aisha, I'm the AE on the account. Marcus, you want to quick intro?
[00:08] Marcus: Yeah hi, Marcus Li, solutions engineer — I work on throughput and private deploys, will jump into technical bits.
[00:13] Priya: Thanks. Priya here, Head of Platform at Halo. We've got Liam and Carlos on for context.
[00:18] Liam: Hi.
[00:19] Carlos: Hey all.
[00:20] Aisha: Great. Goal for today: understand your use case, current stack, and get you to a confident next step — ideally fast time-to-first-token with our PLG quickstart and trial credits.
[00:30] Priya: Sounds good. Quick background: we're building an internal assistant for sales ops and some customer support triage. We want a hosted API to iterate quickly but might need dedicated or private later for PII and compliance. Our infra is on AWS, VPCs, we use Okta for SSO and have strict audit requirements.
[00:47] Aisha: Totally. Typical flow we see: teams start on hosted Redwood API with PLG quickstart — free credits, SDKs — get to first token in minutes, then if they need predictable throughput or data isolation they can move to Dedicated, or Private if on-prem/VPC isolation is must.
[01:05] Carlos: What's the difference operationally — like what are the triggers you'd recommend for moving off hosted?
[01:12] Marcus: Good question. Hosted is fastest to get going — we provide API keys, SDKs, streaming. If you're hitting predictable high QPS or need guaranteed latency, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and SLA. Private is for customer-managed control plane, VPC peering and on-prem packages. Typical triggers are compliance (data residency, audit), throughput cost curve, or strict egress policies.
[01:36] Liam: On the PLG side — what is time-to-first-token? How long does it take to get a dev up and running?
[01:41] Aisha: For most teams it's under 15 minutes to get a token and run a basic generate or embeddings call. We'll enable trial credits — we'll set you up with $500 credits and a step-by-step quickstart. Marcus will share a sample prompt set and curl/SDK snippets.
[01:55] Priya: Nice. Two questions: security — do you have SOC 2? And can we get an artifact pack?
[02:02] Marcus: Yes SOC 2 Type II, and we have ISO summaries. We'll send the security pack. For Private we support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs at token/request level. Note: some auto-transcription in support artifacts may mislabel product names, apologies for that.
[02:20] Carlos: Ok, good. For latency — our SLA for the assistant will be p95 under 200ms for short responses (under 128 tokens). Can Redwood hit that on hosted?
[02:32] Marcus: Hosted p95 depends on model and region. For smaller context models and good region proximity, you can get sub-200ms p95 for short replies. If you need that consistently at scale, Dedicated lets you pin GPU capacity and get much more predictable latency. We also do smart routing and KV/prefix caching which helps with repeated queries.
[02:51] Liam: When you say models — can we bring our own, or do we use your catalog?
[02:55] Aisha: We host a curated catalog of open models and Redwood-verified profiles; you can also request model onboarding. For Private deployments, bringing customer models is more common.
[03:05] Priya: Cost — rough ballpark for dedicated? We need to forecast monthly.
[03:09] Aisha: We'll send a pricing sheet. Quick rule of thumb: Dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity. Depends on GPU SKU, throughput targets, and batching. We also recommend Redwood Optimize suggestions like quantization to lower unit costs. We'll include a cost estimator.
[03:23] Marcus: Also worth noting, our platform exposes token-level cost breakdowns per route, so you can monitor and attribute costs per team. That usually helps with chargeback.
[03:33] Carlos: Good. Now, actual integration — is the SDK ready for Go/Node/Python?
[03:37] Marcus: Yes official SDKs for Python, Node, Go; and HTTP REST. We'll share example repo. For streaming responses and function/tool calling, we have examples too.
[03:48] Priya: About data retention — do you keep request data? We need to ensure we can opt out for certain endpoints.
[03:54] Aisha: Hosted by default keeps short-term logs for debugging but you can configure retention policies; for sensitive workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed retention and optional log forwarding to your SIEM. We'll include how retention settings work.
[04:10] Liam: Any pitfalls in the quickstart? Like RBAC or rate-limiting surprises?
[04:15] Marcus: Not really, but common hiccups: forgetting to set CORS or misconfiguring IAM roles when using cross-account access for Dedicated. For PLG, devs sometimes forget to rotate keys after demo. We'll give a checklist.
[04:27] Priya: Who typically owns the security review on your side — we might need a deeper compliance packet for our legal team.
[04:33] Aisha: Our Security & Compliance team owns the packet; I'll attach SOC2 folder and our standard data processing addendum. If you want, we can schedule a separate security deep dive with our security engineer.
[04:45] Carlos: Please do — we have procurement timelines and legal depend on that.
[04:49] Aisha: Noted.
[05:00] Marcus: Liam, curious — what's your target volume? rough qps and token counts?
[05:06] Liam: For phase 1 internal assistant, maybe 20 concurrent users, spikes to 200 during demos, each request ~100 tokens. Long term could be thousands of users.
[05:17] Marcus: For bursty patterns we recommend Dedicated with burst capacity; for phase 1 you can stay hosted and use automatic batching and caching. You'll want to set per-route rate-limits and caching TTLs. Also, prefix caching for repeated conversation starts reduces cost significantly.
[05:31] Liam: Do you do KV cache management for chat workloads? How much of the state is cached?
[05:36] Marcus: We have automatic KV cache for repeated prefixes and can pin session context in memory for Dedicated. For hosted, KV cache is best-effort and depends on sequence lengths; we'll share docs on cache semantics.
[05:48] Liam: For Private — what's the deployment model? VPC peering or full on-prem?
[05:53] Marcus: We support both. Private can be VPC-hosted with peering and customer-managed networking, or an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. KMS integration for keys, and full audit logs.
[06:04] Priya: Ok. Another question: do you provide benchmarks or a standard evaluation harness?
[06:09] Aisha: Yes, we have evaluation harnesses and benchmarking templates. Marcus will propose a small benchmark using your prompt set to measure latency & cost.
[06:17] Carlos: That would help. Also we'd like to compare to Anthropic API latency as a benchmark.
[06:23] Marcus: Sure — we can include comparative runs. One note: model variants and quantization affect latency, so we'll test a couple of configurations.
[07:00] Aisha: Quick on commercial: PLG is free to start, we enable trial credits. If you go Dedicated, we have reserved capacity pricing and enterprise SLA add-ons. For Private there's a platform fee plus support. We'll tailor a proposal after the pilot.
[07:17] Priya: Great — procurement and legal will need the DPA and SOC2 artifacts.
[07:21] Aisha: We'll send those.
[07:23] Liam: Can you enable a sandbox project for us? Prefer separate dev org.
[07:27] Aisha: Yes — we'll create a sandbox org, enable $500 credits, and invite the three of you.
[07:33] Carlos: Timeline — we want a pilot in the next two weeks. Is that reasonable?
[07:37] Marcus: Yes. We'll prepare a benchmark plan and target 1-week run to collect metrics.
[07:44] Aisha: Quick recap: Redwood to send quickstart guide, trial credits, security pack, SDK examples, and pricing sheet. Marcus to send benchmark plan and sample prompt set. Halo to share workloads and acceptance criteria. We'll schedule the benchmark call, target next Thursday for the technical run.
[08:23] Priya: I'll share the prompt sets and SLA notes by Monday.
[08:27] Aisha: Perfect. Any final Qs?
[08:30] Carlos: None from me.
[08:31] Liam: All good.
[08:32] Aisha: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with links.
[08:36] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: speaker turn-taking is accurate overall; occasional misrecognitions of product names (e.g., "KV cache" spelled as "K-V cache"), and some filler words left in.

References shared: Quickstart repo link (sent later), security pack (will be attached), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared).
